import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Extract the relevant variables for analysis
education_expenditure = adjusted_savings_df.iloc[:, 2:].values
gni_per_capita = gni_per_capita_df.iloc[:, 2:].values
exports_growth = exports_df.iloc[:, 2:].values

# Calculate the correlation between education expenditure and per capita GDP
correlation_matrix = np.corrcoef(education_expenditure, gni_per_capita)
correlation_education_gni = correlation_matrix[:education_expenditure.shape[1], education_expenditure.shape[1]:]

# Calculate the correlation between per capita GDP and economic output (exports growth)
correlation_gni_exports = np.corrcoef(gni_per_capita, exports_growth)
correlation_gni_exports = correlation_gni_exports[:gni_per_capita.shape[1], gni_per_capita.shape[1]:]

# Display the correlation matrices
correlation_education_gni, correlation_gni_exports

# Melt the datasets to have a long format suitable for analysis
adjusted_savings_melted = adjusted_savings_df.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code'], var_name='Year', value_name='Education_Expenditure')
gni_per_capita_melted = gni_per_capita_df.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code'], var_name='Year', value_name='GNI_per_capita')
exports_melted = exports_df.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code'], var_name='Year', value_name='Exports_Growth')

# Merge the datasets on 'Year' and 'Country Group'
merged_data = pd.merge(adjusted_savings_melted, gni_per_capita_melted, on=['Country Group', 'Year'])
merged_data = pd.merge(merged_data, exports_melted, on=['Country Group', 'Year'])

# Display the first few rows of the merged dataset
merged_data.head()
